Hannah — read their redline. We should avoid an absolute prohibition on training; that would materially impair platform improvements and increases friction for most customers. Proposed path (legal):

1) Keep customer ownership of raw inputs and Outputs — acceptable language confirming HarborAI retains title to Outputs it receives.

2) Carve a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free "Feedback License": Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified Feedback and Telemetry for the purpose of improving and operating the Redwood service, provided that such Feedback does not include Customer Content or Outputs in a form that is identifiable to HarborAI or its end users.

3) Add a strict prohibition: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or update model weights in a manner that would create a derivative model created from HarborAI-specific content.

4) Operational opt-out: Allow HarborAI to opt out of any inclusion of their Outputs in training datasets (i.e., full training opt-out). If they opt out, apply a pricing uplift. We suggest 8-12% uplift; ops should confirm estimate.

5) Audit & notice: propose a 30 day notice before any change in how aggregated telemetry is used for model updates.

I can prepare a tracked-changes counter and a short cover email. Let me know if Sales is comfortable with the 8-12% uplift range if they choose opt-out.

— Marcus

Quick ops read: implementing a per-customer training opt-out is feasible. Operational impacts:

- We can tag HarborAI traffic and ensure it is excluded from model-training pipelines and long-term KV caches used for model improvements.
- That will increase per-token servicing cost slightly (fewer aggregation efficiencies) and reduce our ability to proactively fix model drift for that tenant.
- Estimated recommended uplift: 10% (middle of Marcus' range) to compensate for lost telemetry and added isolation controls. If Sales wants a lower uplift we can do 7% but will need manual monitoring for a while.

I also recommend a brief SLA note: when opt-out is enabled, we exclude their traffic from our continuous improvement window and will provide monthly model-quality summaries for visibility.

— Naomi

Subject: RE: HarborAI redlines to MSA (training & output ownership) — compromise proposal

Hi Jill / Samir — thanks for the clear redline. We appreciate HarborAI's desire to retain Output ownership. To move forward quickly we propose the following compromise (summary below; tracked changes attached in a short counter):

- Ownership: HarborAI retains ownership of Customer Content and any Outputs delivered to HarborAI under the Order Form.
- Feedback license: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and feedback for product improvements. We will not use identifiable Customer Content or Outputs to train or produce derivative models.
- Training opt-out: HarborAI may elect a per-tenant training opt-out. If elected, Redwood will exclude HarborAI traffic from model-training pipelines and certain long-term caches. The opt-out will be reflected in the Order Form and carry a 10% price uplift.
- Notice & audit: Redwood will provide 30 days' notice of material changes to telemetry usage and will provide quarterly summaries of aggregated quality metrics upon request.

We attached a concise counter (HarborAI_MSA_redline_counter.docx) with tracked changes and a single-column clean copy for signature. If this looks acceptable we can circulate a DocuSign envelope tonight and aim for signature next week.

Attachments: HarborAI_MSA_redline_counter.docx (proposed language)

Would you be open to the opt-out with the 10% uplift? Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah — appreciate the rapid turnaround and the specificity. HarborAI legal reviewed Marcus' suggested language and the opt-out proposal. We can accept the proposed compromise with the following small edits:

- Clarify that "aggregated, de-identified" excludes any verbatim Outputs or logs linked to an identifiable tenant.
- Add a provision that if HarborAI later authorizes use of Outputs for targeted model training, such authorization must be recorded by written amendment to the Order Form.

With those clarifications we are happy to sign. Please send the DocuSign link and we will route internally this week.

Thanks — Jill
